Anja Kaiser, Balance presents Siren poster, Club Culture Festival 2017

A lilac festival poster with a sharp blackletter “Balance pres.”, wide and stretched sans-serif names, an op-art ray disk, and blurred black shapes.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia
Creator
Anja Kaiser
Made
2017 (the poster reads “May 12, ’17”)
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Dense, experimental, nocturnal
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px image Anja-Kaiser-Balance-p-Siren-Poster.jpg that Eye on Design published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. The object is a digital image as the magazine published it, not a named physical copy. The caption reads “Anja Kaiser, Balance Presents Siren Poster”.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Eye on Design shows the poster in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Anja Kaiser, Balance Presents Siren Poster”.

The poster text names the Club Culture Festival, Institut fuer Zukunft in Leipzig, Laurel Halo, and The Empire Line, and lists the funders, among them the European Commission and the Kulturstiftung des Freistaates Sachsen.

Observed

  • The ground is a flat pale lilac with a black frame.
  • “Balance pres.” is set very large in a sharp, angular blackletter at the top.
  • Performer names are set in a wide, horizontally stretched sans-serif in capitals. The date and venue run vertically down the right edge.
  • A black-and-white disk of radiating lines with a small checkered center sits in the middle, like an op-art target.
  • Motion-blurred black marks and a faint, gray 3D-rendered form overlap the type.
  • Small text, logos, and notes fill the lower edge.

Why it belongs

The poster has the typographic grammar of the trend, blackletter against stretched grotesques with an op-art figure, without its chrome or black ground. It shows that the name covers a wider club-poster practice than the chrome core.

Borrow

Combine one blackletter line with names in a horizontally stretched grotesque.

Use a radial op-art disk as the central image of a type-led poster.
